title: NOX METALS vs OnlineMetals.com for Aluminum Plate (2026 Comparison)
summary: OnlineMetals.com publishes a cut tolerance of plus or minus 0.125 inch and a free mill test report. NOX METALS holds tighter tolerances on thick plate and ships DFARS melt-source documentation by default. An honest comparison of where each one wins.
body_markdown:
### Is NOX METALS cheaper than OnlineMetals.com?


It depends on the piece. On a small cut of common 6061 the two are usually close, and OnlineMetals charges no cut fee. On thick plate and on anything that fits an existing certified drop in our inventory we are typically well below cut-to-size pricing, often by 20 to 40 percent on the drop. Run both quotes: ours takes under 60 seconds.


### What is OnlineMetals cut tolerance?


OnlineMetals publishes a cut tolerance of plus or minus 0.125 inch on long and sheet products unless otherwise specified. Plan your facing stock around that figure if you order from them.


### Does OnlineMetals provide mill certs?


Yes. They include a free printed mill test report on qualifying material when you check the MTR box at checkout. Note that an MTR documents chemistry and mechanical properties, which is not the same as melt-source documentation for a DFARS flow-down.


### Who has better aerospace aluminum, NOX METALS or OnlineMetals?


Both stock 7050-T7451 and reference AMS 4050, so availability is genuinely competitive. The difference is the documentation and the thickness strategy: we ship DFARS-compliant and domestic-melt material with heat-number traceability by default and cut thick sections to size, and we commit to a ship date before you order.


### Does either company sell laser-cut parts?


No. Both of us sell stock material. If you need a finished flat part with holes and profiles, you want a parts-cutting service, and a good number of those shops buy their raw plate from suppliers like us.
